A reason to return.
A battle you can finish later.

Two authored boss hunts, six earned hero paths, and three tier-six Mythics. Exact battle recovery lets you leave and continue after reloading.

01 / Earn choices through play

Hunts first, mastery after.

25

Enter the hunts

Account level 25 or a Tidereach clear opens both encounters. Choose Casual, Normal, or Veteran.

1 → 2

Shape each champion

Win one distinct hunt with a hero for their first path. Win both for the second. Casual counts; equipping and switching are free before a battle.

30

Forge a Mythic

Master both hunts on Normal or Veteran with the tower family. A standing tier-five-or-higher tower must deal 4,000 damage. Stamps can be earned before level 30.

The account cap stays at 40. The release puts concrete challenges and different abilities after Seraph, rather than adding an empty climb to level 50.

02 / Two different tactical problems

Defeat the procession. Bring down the crown.

The Bone Procession

The Ossuary raises fallen escorts within three tiles. Focus the boss, or defeat escorts outside its green circle. Raised units pay no bounty.

The Fallen Crown

Air towers break the Empress's wings. A grounded armored phase follows. Strongest targeting opens that second phase earlier, while other towers manage her escorts.

Both encounters are ten waves, around 11–13 minutes without early calls. They introduce bosses previously buried in deep endless play through authored waves and explicit briefings. Boss leaks fail the hunt.

These captures use the actual renderer with staged enemy placement, gold and unlocks. They show presentation, not evidence that a build can afford its towers or win.

03 / Tier VI

Three transformations. One shared slot.

Helios Engine · +15,000 gold

Seven independent beams charge a telegraphed solar strike. Eighty-four hits release a 2,400 true-damage area attack; moving foes can escape the warning.

Event Horizon · +16,000 gold

A timed rift reveals phased enemies and gives the whole defense a 30% damage window. The dark orbital silhouette keeps the Void branch distinct.

Last Legion · +14,000 gold

The Oathgate Citadel becomes a four-soldier legion. Plant its standard at the rally point to regroup and fully restore the squad, then sustain nearby allies for seven seconds. Cooldown: 24 seconds.

One Mythic may stand per defense, including co-op. Selling it frees the slot. Other tower branches keep their tier-five ceiling.

Seraph Mythics need an extended battle's economy: their full upgrade chains cost over 30,000 gold, above a short hunt's roughly 19,400–20,000 income. Hunts fund the tier-five mastery challenge; Last Legion can fit their budget.

04 / Come back to your battle

Save & exit. Reload. Continue.

Exact local battle recovery

Campaign, endless, and solo hunts autosave every five seconds and when the page hides. Save & exit records the current moment. Continue restores paused, including current enemies, projectiles, tower damage, hero upgrades and temporary abilities.

Battle saves stay on this browser/device. Account progress is what syncs across devices. Co-op and competitive challenge modes do not support mid-battle resume.

Recovery details and limits

A frozen starting loadout and ordered command journal replay the real simulation without duplicating account rewards. Long battles take longer to reconstruct and show progress. A ruleset update may invalidate an older battle; mismatched or failed recovery data is kept and explained. The journal is bounded at 12 simulated hours or 20,000 orders.

Google sign-in, without save codes

The primary account action becomes Sign in with Google. Existing local progress and legacy cloud saves are preserved. File backups and recovery of old codes remain tucked under Backups & older saves.

Production setup still required: configure Google's Web OAuth client and add GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET to Fly. The button stays disabled until the backend advertises readiness.

Callback: https://blockhold-sync.fly.dev/v1/auth/google/callback

05 / Actual combat evidence

Normal supports four different defenses.

Forty-eight actual Game simulations: two hunts × three difficulties × four purchase plans × two seeds. All use account level 25, base Aldric, no Armory, no hero paths, and no Mythics. Gold comes from authored income.

HuntCasualNormalVeteran
Bone Procession8 / 8 wins8 / 8 wins8 / 8 wins
Fallen Crown8 / 8 wins8 / 8 wins3 / 8 wins

Builds cover mixed towers, precision archers/ballistae, Barracks with ranged support, and a Solar Seraph with support. Both Normal hunts have demonstrated Seraph and Barracks mastery routes.

These are scripted outcomes, not predicted player win rates. Frequent ability use and efficient buying favor the simulation. Only two seeds are sampled. The Empress particularly rewards switching to Strongest: four Normal mixed/Barracks losses on First became four wins with the targeting change. Human testing still needs to assess encounter feel and readability under pressure.

Verification and repeatable evidence
  • 318 game tests, 43 server tests and 15 browser smoke checks passed. Typechecks, ESLint, production build and the compressed bundle budget also passed.
  • Recovery checks: active hero field, delayed meteors, final-tick inputs, campaign victory into endless, and honestly purchased Last Legion through active standard expiry and future combat.
  • Authentication checks use real HTTP routes with isolated SQLite and a mock Google transport. Real Google login requires the configured provider.
  • Reproduce combat using scripts/hunt-audit.mjs; raw purchases, outcomes and damage appear in reviews/hunt-balance.json.
Review uses Blockhold's existing wood, parchment, gold and blue palette. Screenshots and motion clips come from its own Three.js renderer. Auth setup instructions: server/AUTH.md. Detailed balance evidence: reviews/hunt-balance.md.
